items.title: Buddhism has no creator god
items.claim: Does Buddhism teach the existence of a supreme creator deity?

options.text: Yes, the Buddha is the supreme deity worshipped as such
No — classical Buddhism rejects an eternal creator god; gods (devas) may exist but are themselves caught in samsara
Yes, Brahma is the Buddhist supreme being
Only Mahayana Buddhism affirms a creator god

items.reveal:
In the Pali Canon, the Buddha refuses metaphysical speculation about a creator (e.g. the Aggi-Vacchagotta Sutta, the 'parable of the poisoned arrow'). Devas exist but are impermanent and themselves seek liberation. The path to nibbana does not depend on grace from a supreme being.

Later traditions (Pure Land, some Mahayana schools) develop devotional practice toward Buddhas and bodhisattvas, but these are still not creators in the Abrahamic sense.

The Buddha is not a god — he is an awakened human teacher.
items.why: Western religious frameworks define 'religion' through theism. Buddhism is a major world tradition that fits awkwardly inside that frame — and forces a rethink of what 'religion' even means.

items.title: Joseph Fletcher's situation ethics centres on agape
items.claim: What is the central principle of Fletcher's situation ethics?

options.text: There are no moral rules whatsoever
The single absolute is agape (selfless love); all other rules are guidelines that can be overridden when love requires. Set out in 'Situation Ethics: The New Morality' (1966)
Maximise pleasure for the greatest number

items.reveal:
Fletcher's six propositions: (1) Only love is intrinsically good. (2) The ruling norm of Christian decision is love, not law. (3) Love and justice are the same — justice is love distributed. (4) Love wills the neighbour's good. (5) Only the end justifies the means. (6) Love's decisions are made situationally, not prescriptively.

Fletcher's four working principles: pragmatism, relativism, positivism, personalism.

The Vatican condemned situation ethics under Pius XII (1956, before Fletcher's book) and again in the 1990s. Critics argue 'love' as sole criterion is too vague; defenders argue agape has specific New Testament content that excludes self-interested 'love'.
items.why: Christian ethics in the mid-20th century split between absolutist and contextual approaches. Fletcher's situation ethics is a high-profile example of context-driven ethics — challenging the natural law tradition from within Christianity.

items.title: Diwali has multiple regional meanings

options.text: A single event — Rama's return to Ayodhya

Multiple events depending on region: Rama's return to Ayodhya (north India), Krishna's defeat of Narakasura (south India), Lakshmi's emergence (west India); also marks new year for some Hindu, Jain and Sikh communities

items.reveal:
Diwali (Sanskrit dipavali, 'row of lamps') falls in October-November on the new moon of Kartika. The five-day festival includes Dhanteras (wealth), Naraka Chaturdashi (Krishna's victory), Diwali itself (Lakshmi puja, Rama's return), Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj (siblings).

For Jains, it marks Mahavira's attainment of moksha. For Sikhs, it commemorates Guru Hargobind's release from imprisonment in 1619 (Bandi Chhor Divas).

The festival has become a major UK public event — Leicester's Diwali celebrations are the largest outside India.
items.why: Pan-Hindu festivals can have different narratives in different regions. Treating Diwali as a single myth misses how diverse Hindu practice is and how it links to neighbouring traditions (Jain, Sikh) at the same calendrical moment.
